_comment: Cleanup-discard BUCKET policy (StompyProvider; MTG_STOMPY_BUCKET_DISCARD=0 restores the generic highest-MV base and fails this fixture). Turn 3 ends with 11 cards after the elf casts, so cleanup sheds FOUR. The generic MV rule sheds Worldspine, Worldspine, Terastodon -- and then Craterhoof, the deck's only copy, with an all-Forest library offering no reprint: the T5 hoof kill dies in the discard. The bucket policy sheds the three excess Forests (board is already at 6+ sources) and one spare threat instead, keeping the hoof for the turn-5 hard cast (9 sources by T5, 4 elf bodies -> lethal swing). Depth 0 ON PURPOSE: at d>0 the searched cleanup pass rescues the hoof in BOTH arms (a trial rollout sees the lost win inside the horizon), so only greedy exposes the ranking itself -- which is exactly what rollout-internal cleanups and beyond-horizon ties consume. USER 2026-08-21: buckets <mana> <threats> <enablers>; threats in hand are spares ('you can fetch to top of deck with Worldly Tutor and drop it off the top') but the LAST hoof-role copy anywhere is kept -- pitching it kills every fetch route to it.
